title: Merged behaviour catalog
description: The deliverable of Phase 0's reference research: one row per behaviour, merged across the repos that had it. A row separates what the behaviour **is** -- committed in our own words -- from how a particular repo **spelled** it, which is expression and is withheld unless every source grants reuse. `license`, `reuse_status` and `obligations` are derived from the code halves of `licenses.yaml` and are present so that a hand-written value can be contradicted by the derivation table rather than merely ignored.

change_notice.description: Populated when any row is adapted from a source under a licence requiring `state_changes`, and it names what changed and whom to credit. Null when no such source contributed: the notice is an obligation attached to specific sources, not a blanket disclaimer.

id.description: Unique across the file. Duplicate ids fail validation naming the id; uniqueness is a cross-record rule and so is the validator's.

description.description: In our own words, never a source's. An empty description fails naming the row.

source_repos.description: Every repo the behaviour was found in. A single-source row classified `generic` must also appear in `overlap_exceptions.yaml`, because one repo's opinion is not corroboration.

required_slots.description: Every entry must be available to the row's scope -- a slot some room type provides for `room`, or one the `house` scope provides for `house`. Checked by the validator, which can read `room_types.yaml` and this file together. The entry shape is the runtime `slot` schema's own `name` property, referenced rather than restated: a restated slot pattern is a second definition free to drift from the published one, and named-slot shapes are what task 7.6's conformance check exists to catch.

concept.description: What the behaviour means, always populated and always in our own words. This is the half of the row that is ours even when every source withholds reuse.

expression.description: How a source spelled it. Must be empty unless every source repo's **code** reuse status is `reusable`; populated while any source is non-granting fails validation. Deliberately permitted to be null rather than omitted: the field's presence with a null value is the record that the question was asked.

raw_ids.description: The raw records this row was derived from. Every shipped row cites at least one, and an empty list fails naming the row: a row with no provenance cannot be audited against the licence whose statuses it carries.

license.description: The most restrictive source **code** licence under the published order. A licence value, never a status.

obligations.description: The union of the source code licences' obligations. A union rather than the strictest single source's list, because an obligation is a thing we must do and dropping one because another source did not impose it would be self-serving.

retention.description: `audit` on a `discard` row and null otherwise. A discarded personal behaviour is retained for audit rather than deleted: it is the record that we saw it and why it did not ship.

change_notice.description: Non-null, naming what changed and whom to credit, when a source imposes `state_changes`; null otherwise.
